toml:
# Xona Pulsar X1 and X5 over one pass, with the Pulsar constellation's highest passes.
#
# A maritime user in the Bay of Biscay (moving at 8 m/s, heading east) sees a designed pass of a
# Pulsar satellite at the full-constellation altitude of 1080 km and 53 deg inclination
# peaking at 70 deg, and the four highest passes of the inclined Pulsar shell (192 satellites,
# 12 planes, Walker phasing 1) built by the constellation-design code, next to GPS L1 C/A.
#
# Every Pulsar signal number is public: Leclere, Marathe and Reid, ION GNSS+ 2025,
# https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.19551, Tables 1 and 2 (X1 at 1593.3225 MHz, 1.023 Mchip/s; X5 at
# 1190.51625 MHz, 10.23 Mchip/s; received power -148.2 to -139.1 dBW on X1 and -144.9 to
# -136.2 dBW on X5). The paper gives received powers, not an EIRP or a pattern: the preset
# takes a flat pattern and the EIRP that delivers the published minimum at 10 deg elevation.
# The maximum carrier Doppler a static user can see from each orbit (33.6 kHz on X1 for the
# polar shell, 31.8 kHz for the inclined one) is validated against the paper's Table 1.
#
# MODELLED as a whole: the pattern and EIRP are inferred from the published powers.
kind = "leo-pass"
name = "Xona Pulsar pass"
epoch = "2026-09-28T10:00:00"
duration_s = 1200.0
step_s = 5.0

[user]
environment = "maritime"
lat_deg = 45.5
lon_deg = -5.0
height_m = 10.0
speed_m_s = 8.0
heading_deg = 90.0

[[satellite]]
id = "Pulsar-pass"
system = "xona-pulsar"
altitude_km = 1080.0
inclination_deg = 53.0
max_elevation_deg = 70.0
tca_s = 600.0

[[leo_constellation]]
system = "xona-pulsar"
max_satellites = 4

[leo_constellation.design]
name = "Pulsar inclined"

[[leo_constellation.design.shell]]
total = 192
planes = 12
phasing = 1
altitude_km = 1080.0
inclination_deg = 53.0

[gnss]
constellation = "gps-baseline"
band = "L1"
